newsitem.title: GERMANY: Waigel confident EMU stability pact to be passed.
newsitem.headline: Waigel confident EMU stability pact to be passed.

text.p: Finance Minister Theo Waigel said on Wednesday he was confident the European monetary union stability pact would be passed soon and that Germany would meet the criteria for EMU.
"I am confident that the stability pact will finally be approved shortly," Waigel said at an industry symposium.
Waigel added however that the degree of economic convergence of prospective EMU participants would determine the time plan and that the criteria must be strictly applied.

"It is understandable that the new French government wanted time to think," Waigel said. "If France wants to put greater emphasis on employment policies on the European level, we are prepared to discuss concrete proposals."
The stability pact itself, however, will not be renegotiated, he said.
Waigel said the stability criteria were more important than the January 1999 start date for EMU. "Convergence determines the schedule -- for every single country," he said.
"The German government believes it is absolutely necessary that the treaty rules be strictly applied in the convergence evaluation," Waigel said.

Despite official estimates showing an 18 billion mark shortfall in tax revenues, Waigel said "It will be possible to meet the three percent deficit criterion...We will do everything so that Germany fulfils the convergence criteria in 1997."
